title: National Memorial Arboretum — 49 Squadron Memorial
memorial_address: National Memorial Arboretum, Croxall Road, Alrewas, Staffordshire DE13 7AR
narrative: 49 Squadron RAF flew Manchester and Lancaster bombers during World War Two from stations including Scampton, Fiskerton, and Syerston in Lincolnshire and Nottinghamshire. The squadron suffered heavy losses throughout the strategic bombing campaign. The NMA hosts memorials to many RAF Bomber Command squadrons and units, grouped within its Bomber Command area. The 49 Squadron Association remains active, returning annually to the former airfield sites at Fiskerton and Scampton for Remembrance services.
memorial_details:
Memorial stone within the Bomber Command memorial area of the National Memorial Arboretum, Croxall Road, Alrewas, Staffordshire DE13 7AR. Dedicated 2018. The NMA is open year-round. 49 Squadron Association maintains close connection to this memorial and to the Fiskerton and Scampton memorial sites.

The memorial stone at the National Memorial Arboretum — the UK's primary centre of remembrance, set within 150 acres of grounds in Staffordshire — was dedicated in 2018, reflecting the enduring activity of the 49 Squadron Association.

external_narratives.summary: 49 Squadron Association memorials page documenting the NMA stone dedicated in 2018 and the association's ongoing connection to memorial sites at Fiskerton and Scampton.
